notes:
Summary: engaged on Dedicated capacity + Private deployment. Enterprise financial customer (trading platform) with strict latency and residency needs. Primary ask: reserved GPU pool for low-latency chat & reranking during market hours; explicit throughput guarantees and clear SLA credits.

Key requirements:
- Workloads: chat (agent workflows for traders), reranking for search, embeddings for doc search, summarization of financial reports.
- Latency targets: p95 < 150ms for short-turn chat responses (up to 512 tokens), p99 tail < 300ms during peak hours.
- Throughput targets: sustain 200 req/s baseline, spike to 800 req/s for 30-60s bursts during market opens; require autoscaling/burst policy for Dedicated.
- Reserved planning: spec requested for 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (option to scale to 16 for peak), prefer dedicated pool with isolation.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to commit to annual reserved capacity for discounts but need predictable unit economics.

POC / Evaluation plan:
- 2026-02-20: start 2-week perf POC on Dedicated hardware (Redwood provides 2-week eval capacity).
- Deliverables: throughput/latency report, kv/prefix caching impact analysis, cost projection for reserved vs burst capacity.
- Success criteria: meet p95/p99 SLOs for defined request mix and demonstrate price/performance advantage over current cloud GPU infra.

Procurement & Legal:
- Orion procurement raised DPA/MSA redlines: stronger data residency clauses, customer-controlled key lifecycle, and expanded termination rights tied to incident thresholds.
- Insurance: procurement requests proof of cyber liability insurance >= $5M; Redwood standard certificate not sufficient per their broker.
- Compliance add-ons: Orion requires additional audit logging retention (7 years) and custom retention controls; legal says this may require a separate addendum that affects SLA (longer posture for on-prem or Private).
- SLA negotiation: Orion legal pushing for 99.99% uptime on Dedicated with financial credits; Redwood needs to clarify carve-outs for scheduled maintenance, emergency security patches, and compliance-driven downtime.

Quote / Commercials:
- AE provided preliminary reserved quote for 8x A100-equivalent capacity + 24/7 support + compliance add-on. Customer requests line-items: SLA credits, indemnity cap adjustments, insurance attachments.

Internal notes / Risks:
- High chance deal requires legal + risk + security meeting to sign off on DPA/MSA redlines.
- Compliance add-on may increase cost and reduce committed availability window — needs engineering ops confirmation.
- Timeline: procurement expects final MSA + insurance proof before 2026-04 to hit internal budget cycle.

Customer quotes:
- "We need guarantees during market open — latency spikes are not acceptable." — Head of Infrastructure (Orion)
- "If the compliance add-on forces extended maintenance windows, we can't accept the current SLA figure." — Procurement lead

Next actions:
- Schedule SLA workshop (legal + infra + AE + SE) week of 2026-03-03.
- SE to deliver detailed reserved-GPU sizing + cost sheet by 2026-03-05.
- AE to obtain updated cyber insurance certificate from Redwood risk team and submit to Orion procurement.
